# Independent audit: prepared dirty membership

Scope: read-only review of the staged files under `.cache/prepared-dirty-membership/proposed/src/` and `implementation.patch`. The staged patch is not applied to `src/`. I did not run tests or alter runtime files. Line references below point to the staged copies.

## Conclusion

The revised staged patch adds a post-functional-action guard in `#dispatchState`; with that guard, the identity-only native acknowledgement shortcut is justified by the current World lifecycle. The guard rejects an updater result if the owner is no longer live or the owner/site no longer contains the exact captured cell. Without it, exact identity-map membership alone was insufficient; do not apply the earlier staged version.

The private-candidate path does not receive or mark a committed cell’s token before publication. Publication either keeps the existing committed cell and marks that cell’s token after applying a candidate write, or inserts a new candidate cell and creates its token only after insertion. Rollback/discard only affect candidate-local data. The numeric row is released before the owner’s membership nodes are removed, so a later row reuse cannot make an old token target the new owner.

## Token provenance and source shape

- `PreparedDirtyMembershipToken` is a module-private class. Its constructor requires the module-private `preparedMembershipAuthority`, and the token stores `#journalIdentity` and `#entry` private fields (`world_dirty_journal.ts:31-50`). The static resolver checks the actual private-field brand with `#entry in value`, then verifies journal identity and that the bucket has not been retired (`:53-67`). There is no reflectable symbol-based dispatch surface. The exposed TypeScript interface’s unique-symbol member is only a compile-time shape; it does not provide runtime authority.
- A token can be forged neither by copying own keys nor by presenting a tuple-shaped object. `Object.freeze` prevents adding public properties, while private slots remain mutable to the class’s `retire` method (`:40-50, :69-81`). The private-brand `in` check does not invoke a proxy’s `getPrototypeOf` trap; the proposed test covers that malformed-proxy case (`prepared_dirty_membership_test.ts:18-77`).
- Each journal has its own identity object (`world_dirty_journal.ts:91-96`). Passing a real token to another journal is declined. Removing an owner marks its bucket retired, clears each token’s private references, clears entry links/map membership, and deletes the owner bucket (`:190-210`). Reusing the same numeric owner key later creates a new bucket; the old token has already been retired and cannot resolve to the new bucket.
- A cell token points to an entry, which points to its bucket, but not to the `WorldDirtyJournal` instance or any state payload (`:3-23, :33-49`). On owner destruction the cell reference is cleared as well (`owner_state_world.ts:1663-1675`). Thus retained dead setters do not keep the journal’s owner/site nodes alive through the cell.

## Ordering and journal lifecycle

- `mark` and `prepareMembership` both use `#entryFor`, so each owner/site has one reusable node (`world_dirty_journal.ts:108-159`). `markPrepared` uses that node directly; repeated marks on an active node coalesce without reordering (`:130-172`).
- Active sites are appended to the owner’s site list and newly active owners are appended to the owner list (`:161-172, :244-263`). Deleting a site unlinks it; if it was the owner’s final active site, the owner is also unlinked. A later mark appends both back at the tail (`:174-188, :265-273`). This matches the prior insertion/deletion ordering.
- `clear` walks the active lists while saving each next pointer before clearing the current node’s links. It deactivates all entries and owners but retains their maps/nodes/tokens for reuse (`:212-233`). Subsequent authenticated marks reactivate entries at the tail. `removeOwner` instead retires tokens and frees the bucket/site map (`:190-210`).
- `has`, `entries`, `size`, `pendingChanges`, and `drainChanges` retain their intended membership semantics: `has` is direct owner/site membership lookup (`:103-106`); enumeration remains owner-major/site insertion order (`:235-242`); `size` tracks active owners (`:98-101`); `clear` is still the operation used by `drainChanges` after materializing pending records (`owner_state_world.ts:1575-1587`).

## World integration, acknowledgement, and reentrancy

- The first committed write obtains a prepared membership node through `#markCellDirty`, stores it on that committed cell, and marks it (`owner_state_world.ts:1685-1693, 1711-1757`). Later writes reuse the same token. Candidate-local dispatch does not call this method; it updates only its candidate cell and candidate-local `hasStateWrites` (`:853-899`).
- Native acknowledgement still checks the exact identity-map entry, handle identity, owner/site provenance, and captured version before deleting membership (`:1537-1559`). The changed operation is the final deletion: it uses the cell’s prepared node rather than repeating owner/site lookup. A captured older version leaves newer writes pending because `entry.cell.version > capturedVersion` skips deletion. Reentrant callback behavior is unchanged because the version gate precedes the deletion.
- **Counterexample against the earlier version:** `#dispatchState` originally asserted owner liveness before invoking a functional action (`:1717-1721`) but did not revalidate afterward. If the action destroyed its owner and returned a changed value, dispatch continued against the dead cell, could recreate a dirty entry and—on first dispatch—create a new identity entry after destruction. For an already-committed cell, destruction removed its old identity entry, but dispatch could still dirty the dead cell. The peer supplied regressions for both cases and numeric row reuse.
- The revised guard records whether the action is functional, invokes it, then—before `Object.is`, writes, version/source changes, dirty marking, identity creation, or notification—checks both `#owners.has(owner)` and `#stateByOwner.get(owner)?.get(site) === cell` (`:1717-1729`). This closes the callback window: a destroyed owner fails the first predicate; replacement/removal of the site cell fails the second. For direct-value actions, there is no user callback between the initial assertion and the internal mutation path, so skipping the extra check does not open this window. With this guard, committed identity entries are created only for an extant exact owner/site cell, are preserved when publication mutates that cell in place (`:1181-1213`), and are removed on owner destruction (`:1643-1675`). There are no other identity-map deletion/replacement paths in the staged source. Therefore the removed owner and state-map membership lookups in native acknowledgement are redundant for liveness, while the captured version, handle owner/site, and identity checks remain necessary. Owner-slot occupancy remains a separate question; the token resolver does not claim that a keyed owner currently occupies a particular child slot.
- `clearChangesThrough` remains on the public owner/site path. It checks membership before the version lookup and keeps the owner-live/version condition (`:1562-1572`); it does not traverse journal entries for membership.

## Candidate copy, publication, rollback, and destruction

- Candidate creation explicitly reads the committed value and creates a new candidate object. The candidate starts with `dirtyMembership: undefined`; even lane-eligible candidates use a separate candidate object and do not share the committed row address (`owner_state_world.ts:692-753`). Candidate dispatch mutates that candidate object only (`:853-899`).
- Rollback replays candidate-local undo actions and truncates the undo journal (`:946-965` and the associated checkpoint state). No World journal operation is part of those undo actions. Discard clears candidate dispatch controls/forwarding and does not add committed membership. This isolates failed, stale, and discarded preparation attempts.
- On publish, private owner records and slots are installed before candidate cells (`:1165-1180`). For an existing committed cell, publication writes candidate value/version into the existing cell and marks that existing cell only when its version changed (`:1181-1213`). For a new cell, the candidate object is inserted first; only then can a versioned candidate be marked (`:1215-1224`). No candidate token is copied onto a committed cell. Post-publication controls stop retaining the candidate cell and forward to the live dispatch (`:1227-1233`).
- `destroyOwner` recursively destroys children, removes the owner from its keyed slot, deletes the owner from the live owner map, removes committed identity entries, releases numeric lanes, clears the cell token/payload/source, deletes the state map, then calls `removeOwner` (`:1643-1675`). The synchronous ordering has no callback between the identity/state deletion and journal retirement. Dead setters fail the live-owner assertion before any later mark (`:1679-1682, :1711-1718`). Numeric row generation advances and the row is cleared/recycled in lane release before this journal cleanup; an old handle/token therefore cannot clear a new owner’s membership after row reuse. The proposed row-reuse regression covers the old-handle acknowledgement case (`prepared_dirty_membership_test.ts:108-169`).

## Test coverage and remaining boundary

The revised six-test staged file covers ordering/reactivation, clear reuse, foreign and removed tokens, proxy/tuple forgery, old-version versus latest-version acknowledgement, destruction/dead-handle behavior, numeric row reuse with generation change, and candidate write/discard isolation. Added updater regressions cover destruction before first identity allocation, destruction after an acknowledged identity exists, and destruction followed by numeric row reuse (`prepared_dirty_membership_test.ts:180-286`). These directly close the earlier counterexample. The peer reports all six staged tests passed; I did not rerun them under this read-only assignment.

The tests do not directly exercise publication of a new private owner/state cell with a pre-publication candidate write, nor rollback after repeated candidate layout metadata updates. The inspected code keeps these paths isolated: the new candidate has no token until it is inserted and marked during publish, and checkpoint undo applies only to candidate-local data. A focused future regression could lock those two publication boundaries, but I found no staged lifecycle defect requiring a code change.
